parsed.why: Thin record: no criminalisation and a 2018 equality guarantee on sexual orientation, but no trans-specific protection or recognition; dated societal stigma, with no documented violence, police or border exposure.

Hostile national document and border regime (X markers ended, sex-as-birth rules, visa refusal and fraud risk), facilities bans and a bathroom arrest, plus custody abuse. Some state protections and courts, but universal exposures dominate.

Self-ID law, anti-discrimination and hate-crime aggravation operating in practice, facility access by self-identification, and high social acceptance. One region repealed local protections, but the national regime and recourse remain strong.

Same-sex conduct decriminalised, but no anti-discrimination law, no legal recognition and a constitutional marriage ban; no documented trans violence, border practice or social climate. Thin data, extrapolated as conservative without active state targeting.

State-tolerated targeting: collective police detentions and public shaming, a vagrancy law treating homosexuality as illness, conversion practices, sexual violence in custody with impunity and criminalised advocacy. Severe risk despite no explicit penal-code ban.
